key_insight: MRI radiomics shows moderate ability to noninvasively predict KRAS mutation status in rectal cancer before treatment planning.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help preoperative molecular stratification when tissue-based testing is limited or delayed.
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies.
Included 7 studies with 1,224 rectal cancer patients.
Compared MRI-based radiomics or AI predictions against molecular testing using a bivariate random-effects model.
evidence_signal: Pooled performance was moderate, with sensitivity 0.736, specificity 0.645, and hierarchical summary AUC 0.754.
watch_item: Clinical use is still limited by between-study heterogeneity and the need for external validation in larger, standardized cohorts.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy of MRI Radiomics for Predicting KRAS Mutation in Rectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
